rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4: "she said in the interview" — antecedent "the customer who nearly left last spring" is in the same sentence; L6 "The agent" continues L4 "an agent"; L8 "Making" is bare noun, closest to vague but resolves to the screen-making of L4. Harm (unresolved referent) absent.
L4-8: no pointer to another file or slide by position; grep for opening/earlier/lecture/module → none. Closest: L6 "The agent mirrors what you bring" is a standalone claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no 'the X you did/saw/caught' backward reference

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-8: three paragraphs carrying a self-contained claim (ask quality sets output quality); not a wait-state slide.

Header L1 "Your taste is the ceiling" vs L8 "Knowing what good looks like did not [get cheap]" — body names taste as the scarce thing and the ceiling on output; header is literally true of the content.

L6-8: closest is L6 "A vague ask gets ... A sharp ask ... gets" (a contrast pair, not a not-X-not-Y-Z) and L8 "Making got cheap. Knowing what good looks like did not." (two-clause contrast, no triple, no retraction). No anaphora triple, no superlative, no number, no verb triplet, no abstraction stack.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L8 "Making got cheap. Knowing what good looks like did not." is the closest to an aphorism kicker (class c), but it adds the cost-of-making vs cost-of-judging contrast, which the header ('taste is the ceiling') and L4-6 (ask quality) do not state; not a restatement of the header, so it earns its slot.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
